newsitem.title: USA: GM won't confirm report of buyer for Delphi plants.
newsitem.headline: GM won't confirm report of buyer for Delphi plants.

text.p: General Motors Corp. on Friday refused to confirm a published report that a Wall Street investment firm has emerged as the lead candidate to buy four parts plants in Michigan and Canada.

The Oakland Press in Pontiac, Mich., reported that Joseph, Littlejohn & Levy, a private investment partnership, was negotiating to buy the facilities, which are part of GM's Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems unit.
Delphi representatives said confidentiality agreements with possible buyers precluded them from commenting on the talks.
"We will not identify the parties invovled," said Delphi spokeswoman Lynda Messina. GM hopes to have the deal closed by the end of 1996.
Last week, GM told employees at a Delphi plant in Flint, Mich., that it had entered into discussions with a potential buyer to purchase all four of the plants.
Sources and other published reports at that time said Canadian auto supplier Magna International Inc. was a leading contender to buy the plants. GM denied those reports.

News that Joseph, Littlejohn & Levy could be the buyer rankled employees because the firm oversaw the closing of a Ypsilanti, Mich., plant and the layoff of 200 workers as part of a $1.1 billion merger it engineered between Hayes Wheels International Inc and Motor Wheel Corp. in March.
But Delphi spokeswoman Cheryl Kilborn said GM was committed to finding a buyer that will provide ongoing job opportunities.

"In those cases where we have identified a business for sale we have found buyers who have dedicated substantial resources to the business, provided a secure livelihood for the employees and contributed significantly to their respective employees," she said in a statement.

In addition to the Flint plant, facilities for sale are a plant in Livonia, Mich., Oshawa, Ontario, and Windsor, Ontario. The plants employ a total of 5,100 hourly workers and make a variety of interior parts, including hinges, door panels, instrument panels, and seat parts.
